name: cli-web-ui-flag
description: Verify --web-ui is registered, launches the engine + webui, serves both over HTTP, and cleans up both child processes on real Ctrl+C and SIGTERM with no orphans. The web UI gets a free port; the launcher picks the engine port itself (first free one from 7433 up, since the developer's live engine holds 7433), so the spec reads it from the web UI's config answer. Ctrl+C is a real PTY signal; SIGTERM goes to this run's launcher only and orphans are looked for among this run's processes (the throwaway HOME), never by a pattern over the whole machine, because the developer's live engine and web UI run beside the test.

steps.title: --web-ui serves engine + webui and shuts down cleanly on real Ctrl+C

steps.command: for i in $(seq 1 60); do cfg=$(curl -fs http://127.0.0.1:{{port}}/api/config) || { sleep 0.5; continue; }; eng=$(printf %s "$cfg" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["engine_url"])') || { sleep 0.5; continue; }; curl -fs "$eng/health" >/dev/null && { echo "${eng##*:}" > "$HOME/engine-port"; echo WEBUI_SIGINT_HEALTH_OK; exit 0; }; sleep 0.5; done; echo WEBUI_SIGINT_HEALTH_FAIL
steps.description: Poll the web UI config, then the engine /health it names, until both respond
engine /health and webui / both respond 200 while running
the launcher started its own engine, not the developer's
launcher, engine and web UI are gone after Ctrl+C

steps.command: E=$(cat "$HOME/engine-port"); for i in $(seq 1 30); do if lsof -nP -iTCP:{{port}} -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1 || lsof -nP -iTCP:$E -sTCP:LISTEN >/dev/null 2>&1; then sleep 0.5; else echo WEBUI_SIGINT_CLEANUP_OK; exit 0; fi; done; echo WEBUI_SIGINT_CLEANUP_FAIL
steps.description: After Ctrl+C: verify both ports are released
both ports are released after Ctrl+C

steps.title: --web-ui serves engine + webui and shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM (e.g. a process manager stopping it)

steps.command: for i in $(seq 1 60); do cfg=$(curl -fs http://127.0.0.1:{{port}}/api/config) || { sleep 0.5; continue; }; eng=$(printf %s "$cfg" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["engine_url"])') || { sleep 0.5; continue; }; curl -fs "$eng/health" >/dev/null && { echo "${eng##*:}" > "$HOME/engine-port"; echo WEBUI_SIGTERM_HEALTH_OK; exit 0; }; sleep 0.5; done; echo WEBUI_SIGTERM_HEALTH_FAIL

engine /health and webui / both respond 200 while running
the launcher started its own engine, not the developer's
